narrative:
The model estimates an 85% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your profile that historically align with employees who end up departing.

Three factors stood out as the strongest drivers of this prediction. First, your total years of professional experience (6–10 years) pushed the prediction most strongly toward leaving. While this is a common range, the model associates it with higher turnover compared with people predicted to stay. Second, the time you have spent in your current role (1–5 years) also contributed noticeably toward predicting departure; this is actually the most frequent tenure bracket among employees the model expects to remain, yet in your specific combination of circumstances it still signals elevated risk. Third, having received other job offers while working here was another clear factor pulling the outcome toward leaving. Only about one in four employees predicted to stay report receiving such external opportunities, so this stands out as a meaningful indicator of potential exit.

Taken together, these elements suggest the organization sees you as experienced enough to be attractive to competitors and already receiving outside interest, which often precedes resignation. 

You and your manager should discuss ways to strengthen your sense of long-term fit and growth within the company, such as clearer promotion paths or expanded responsibilities, to reduce the likelihood of departure.
